title: Skillet Lemon & Herb Chicken
description: Crisp chicken thighs with garlic, thyme, and a bright lemon pan sauce.
imageAlt: Painted skillet of golden chicken thighs with lemon and thyme

nutritionAs.4 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs: 11 ounces roasted chicken thigh meat + 2 ounces roasted chicken skin

nutritionNote: Skin-on thighs are rich: most of their calories come from fat, and a good part of it renders into the pan. So they’re counted as cooked meat and skin: four bone-in thighs weigh about 1½ pounds raw, and with the bone left on the plate and USDA’s 69% roasting yield, that’s about 13 ounces: 11 of meat and 2 of skin, using USDA data for roasted chicken. Only a third of the oil is counted, since the rest stays in the skillet. Leave the skin on the plate and the fat drops much further.
ingredients: 1 lemon, half juiced and half thinly sliced
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the 4 chicken thighs dry and season all over with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Add the thighs skin-side down and cook until the skin is deep golden, about 8–10 minutes. Flip the thighs.
Add the 3 garlic cloves, ½ cup broth, juice from half the lemon, and 4 thyme sprigs around the thighs. Thinly slice the other lemon half and tuck the lemon slices into the pan.

Transfer the skillet to the oven. Roast for about 20–25 minutes, until a thermometer inserted into the thickest part of each thigh reads at least 165°F without touching the bone. Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices around the chicken.
